title: Response Variance Gate — Brain Dump
content:
Quick brain dump on a product control I keep sketching out: Response Variance Gate (working name).

Goal / hypothesis:
- Provide developers a simple knob to trade deterministic/cost-stable outputs vs higher-variance creative outputs while keeping predictable token economics and latency SLOs.
- Hypothesis: Many customers want more predictable unit economics from LLMs but still want occasional high-variance outputs for exploration or novelty. A gate + budgeted sampling strategy will reduce unexpected cost spikes and make rollouts safer.

Problem background (observed pain):
- Customers report variable per-request token usage and downstream UX instability when sampling-heavy configs are used in production.
- Currently toggling top_p/temperature is developer-only and often causes occasional runaway hallucinations, long continuations, or token explosions.
- Hard to A/B safe creative behavior without significant infra/observability work.

Core idea (sketch):
1) API-level parameter: variance_gate: {mode, budget, refill_rate, bucket_size} (high-level only in this doc)
2) Modes:
   - closed (strict deterministic; sampling disabled; fallback to greedy/beam)
   - permissive (allow sampling up to X budget per client/route)
   - adaptive (system allows sampling when confidence/score heuristics indicate safe)
3) Budgeting: unit = sampled_token_count or sampling-events (we should experiment to decide). Budget scoped to API key, model+route, or dedicated pool.
4) Refill policies: time-windowed (e.g., 100 samples per hour) and burst bucket to permit short spikes.
5) Fallback policy: when budget exhausted -> degrade to safer generation (lower temperature, nucleus sampling off) OR route to cheaper baseline model variant.

Why this shape?
- Centralized budget prevents rogue prompts from draining spend or producing extreme outputs.
- Makes cost per customer less spiky and easier to plan for Dedicated customers.
- Allows console + SDK surfaces for gradual enablement (dev -> canary -> production).

User stories / acceptance criteria (working):
- As an app eng, I can set variance_gate.mode on a per-route basis and get deterministic output for sensitive endpoints.
- As a growth PM, I can enable permissive mode for an experimental cohort and see sampling usage broken down in Console.
- As infra, when a customer exceeds budget, requests degrade gracefully and logs show exact reason (budget_exhausted: true).
- As SRE, system-level metrics expose sampled_tokens and budget_utilization with alerts at 80% and 100%.

API design (initial sketch, note: keep surface small):
- request body additions (optional):
   "variance_gate": {"mode":"permissive", "budget":{"unit":"sample_tokens","amount":1000, "window":"1h"}}
- server-side defaults if absent: mode: closed for prod-tier endpoints flagged sensitive, permissive for dev keys by default? need persona discussion.

Console & UX ideas:
- Per-route toggle with slider for budget (visualize as hourly/daily budget).
- Timeline of variance-events, heatmap of sampled token spend.
- Quick rollback button that flips mode -> closed and drains pending permissive sessions.

Telemetry / Metrics we need to collect (for experiments):
- sampled_tokens_per_request, sampling_events, budget_tokens_remaining, fallback_rate, mean_response_latency by mode, customer_cost_change_pct, session_quality_change (NPS/proxy).

Experiments to run (MVP):
- A: Budget unit = sampled_tokens. Measure cost smoothing, UX regressions.
- B: Budget unit = sampling_events (binary: event used or not). Simpler but can be gamed.
- C: Adaptive mode with model confidence signal (logprob heuristics) vs naive random allow. Compare false positive/negative rate.

Implementation notes (runtime & infra):
- Need cheap in-flight budget check at request admission (fast in-process counter or redis). Latency target < 1ms additional.
- For Dedicated customers, budget enforcement must be deterministic and offline-configurable.
- Consider using existing rate-limiter infra with a new metric namespace (sampling.*).
- Rollout: start as middleware in hosted API path before exposing in Dedicated control plane.

Security / compliance considerations:
- Deterministic mode should be audited to ensure sampling isn't happening covertly; require logs flagged with mode and effective_sampling_params.
- For regulated customers, expose an exported audit log showing when sampling occurred and which prompts triggered it.

Open questions / risks:
- How to measure "sampling token" size reliably across model variants (tokenization differences)? (TODO: normalize to base-token metric or model-specific lookup)
- Should sampling budget be charged differently (higher unit price) to reflect higher compute? Might be objectionable; better to surface cost transparency in Console first.
- UX: do we expose per-user (app end-user) budgets? That could be powerful but increases storage complexity.
- Attack surface: adversarial prompts tuned to maximize sampling while minimizing detection. Need heuristics and rate limits.

Cost sketch (very rough):
- Engineering: 2 sprints for core admission + metrics + console minimal UI (~6 weeks).
- SRE: 1 sprint for infra capacity planning and alerting.
- Total: small feature team (2 PM, 2 FE, 2 BE) to ship initial experiment.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Align with pricing team on exposed billing for sampled tokens. (ping: Evan)
- Prototype admission check using existing redis token bucket -> measure p99 additional latency.
- Draft a small UX mock for Console and get feedback from Jordan.
- Write short experiment plan with metrics thresholds (e.g., fallback_rate < 2% and cost smoothing > 20% improvement).

Quick sketch of canary rollout plan:
1) Internal dogfooding: enable permissive with high budget for internal keys.
2) Small external cohort (5 customers) with low churn tolerance. Monitor sampling spend and quality metrics for 2 weeks.
3) Expand to opt-in beta in Console.
4) Flip default to permissive for dev keys only.

Related tickets & refs (for later):
- INF-7823 (budget model), INF-7899 (console sampling charts), PR#1203 (server rate-limiter extension).

Random heuristics notes (ideas to test):
- Allow sampling only if top-1 token logprob < -3.0 (i.e., model uncertain) to prioritize creativity when model is unsure.
- Combine with short-circuit retrieval checks: if retrieval confidence high -> force closed.

This is intentionally fuzzy. Want to get initial reactions before drawing a full spec. Main ask for next sync: decide budget unit (tokens vs events) and whether to scope budgets to API key or route.

-- Sam (notes)
